name: Luxembourg-Findel International Airport
before:
Luxembourg's only international airport, and the only one in the country with a paved runway, about 6 km east of Luxembourg City. It carried over five million passengers in 2024.

Freight is where it punches far above its weight. It is fifth busiest in Europe by cargo tonnage, and both Luxair and Cargolux have their headquarters on the site. All of that runs on a single runway handling around 100,000 movements a year, which is a lot for one strip.

The big change for clients is the tram. Line 1 of the Luxembourg City tramway was extended from Kirchberg to the airport in March 2025, so the terminal now has a direct rail link into the city. Buses 6, 16 and 29 also run into Luxembourg City, and regional line 302 goes over the border to Trier.

There are two terminals. Terminal A, inaugurated in May 2008, is the main one. Terminal B is unusual: it has gates but no check in counters and no arrivals hall, and was built for small aircraft, reopening in 2017 able to handle up to 110 passengers.
after:
Luxembourg's only airport with scheduled flights, and the only one in the country with a paved runway, about 6 km east of Luxembourg City. It handles more than five million passengers a year on a single runway.

The tram is the easy way in: Line 1 runs from the terminal into Luxembourg City. Buses 6, 16 and 29 also run into the city. Regional bus 302 goes over the border to Trier.

There are two terminals. Terminal A is the main one, with check-in and baggage reclaim. Beyond it, Terminal B has gates but no check-in counters or arrivals hall, and is reached through Terminal A.

claims.claim: only airport in Luxembourg with scheduled flights; only one with a paved runway
claims.inAfter: Luxembourg's only airport with scheduled flights, and the only one in the country with a paved runway
claims.note: Was 'Luxembourg's only international airport'. OurAirports lists every Luxembourg airfield: only Findel has scheduled service and a paved (asphalt) runway; the others are grass strips and heliports. 'Only airport with scheduled flights' is what that data shows, and says the same thing to an agent.

claims.claim: fifth busiest in Europe by cargo tonnage; Luxair and Cargolux headquarters on the site

claims.why: The cargo ranking is Wikipedia's alone and sits next to a 2010 world ranking, so its date is unclear. Cargolux's own contact page gives its headquarters as 70 rue de Luxembourg, Sandweiler, which does not say 'at the airport'; Luxair was not checked. Cut rather than half-kept.
